text: Huh, it always has six points. Wait, why six?
As water turns to ice, its molecules only link up at a fixed angle - forming a six-sided crystal structure.
As a snowflake grows, its branches spread out by following that same six-sided crystal structure.
So a snowflake's six sides come from the ice itself - its crystal structure is six-sided from the very start.
But as it grows, the exact branch shape shifts with the temperature and humidity around it.
In fact, a man named Wilson Bentley became the first person to photograph a snowflake up close.
Bentley's own story was that no two snowflakes ever look exactly alike.
